h1: Gagan Deep on the first plant: what an imported brewhouse teaches
title: Gagan Deep and the Imported Brewhouse | Craft Beer School
desc: Hops n Grains brewmaster Gagan Deep on the hard-to-assemble first plant, plus what new brewpub founders should check before buying imported kit.
teaser: The first brewhouse arrived from China in crates and took real work to put together. What founders can learn from the Tricity's first microbrewery.
standfirst: When Hops n Grains opened in Panchkula, its first brewing plant was imported from China and difficult to assemble, its brewmaster Gagan Deep later recalled. Here is what that early experience teaches anyone buying a brewhouse today.
sections:
In 2018 Gagan Deep, the in-house brewmaster at Hops n Grains, told The Tribune that the brewery's original plant was Chinese and that assembling it was difficult. He is in a position to know: he has brewed for the Tricity group founded by Amritanshu Agrawal and Dr Priyanka Gupta since its early years.

Hops n Grains opened in Panchkula, by the founders' account in 2010, as the region's first microbrewery. There were few brewpubs in India then and almost no local support for the kit. Dr S Cariappa, a brewmaster from Bengaluru, was brought in to help set up and commission the plant.
Why the origin of the kit matters less than the support

Chinese, German and Indian fabricators all make good brewhouses today. Brewpubs across India run on all three. The difference that hurts a new brewery is rarely the steel. It is what happens after the crates arrive: drawings that do not match the pipework, a missing gasket size, a control panel nobody locally can repair.

In the early years of Indian craft beer, an imported plant meant an ocean between the brewery and its spare parts. The trade has since grown up, which is exactly what Gagan meant when he said the industry had grown by leaps and bounds. Today there are Indian fabricators, service engineers and consultants. A founder in 2010 had far fewer people to call.
What to ask before you buy

1. Who installs it? Who pays for their travel and stay if installation runs long?
  2. Which spare parts come with the plant? Ask for a list of gaskets, seals, valves and sensors by size and a first set of each.
  3. Who services the chiller, the steam or electric heating and the control panel locally?
  4. Are the drawings final? Do they match your floor, drains and ceiling height?
  5. What does commissioning include: water trials, a cleaning trial and a first brew under supervision?

Our brewhouse commissioning checklist goes through the trials step by step.

One thing has not changed since 2010. In India the brewhouse is the easy purchase. A brewpub needs its excise licence, its premises approvals and its food licence lined up before the plant can brew a single commercial batch. Haryana, Punjab and the Chandigarh administration each have their own rules for microbreweries. Those rules change. Read the current notification for your state or work with a licensing adviser. Our guide to craft beer rules in Haryana explains the process for Panchkula.

Time the plant order to the licence, not the other way round. Ask the fabricator for a delivery date you can move. Keep the installation team's dates loose until the approvals are in hand. A brewhouse sitting in crates for six months while paperwork moves costs money and invites damage. Steel left in a humid store grows surface rust on fittings. Gaskets dry out and crack before they are ever used.
Budget for the brewer, not only the kit

The second lesson from Hops n Grains is about people. The founders hired a senior consultant to commission the plant and kept a resident brewmaster to run it. Years later they still credit both. Many failed brewpubs spent everything on steel and then hired the cheapest brewer they could find.

A good brewer finds the small faults an imported plant hides, like a valve that does not seal fully or a temperature probe that reads two degrees off. A cheap one brews around them until the beer suffers. Our guide on when to hire a consultant brewmaster explains how to split the budget between the two roles.

Hops n Grains has outlasted its difficult first plant, a national highway liquor ban that hit many outlets in 2017 and the Covid closures. It opened a third brewpub in Mohali during the pandemic. Its brewery website now talks about equipment handcrafted in Germany, so the kit has clearly moved on.

The brewmaster stayed. For a founder that is the most useful fact in the whole story. Equipment can be replaced. A brewer who knows your plant, your water and your guests takes years to build.
faqs: What plant did Hops n Grains start with?
Brewmaster Gagan Deep told The Tribune in 2018 that the original plant was Chinese and difficult to assemble. The brewery's website now describes German-made equipment.
Who commissioned the Hops n Grains brewery?
Dr S Cariappa, a Bengaluru brewmaster, helped set up and commission the plant.
What should I check before buying an imported brewhouse?
Who installs and services it locally, which spare parts come with it, whether the drawings match your site and what commissioning trials are included.
